subtopics.title: Mean, Median and Mode for Ungrouped Data

questions.question: For the reading times 10, 13, 16, 16, 19, 22, 24, 27, 33 the mean is:
The median of the nine ordered values is:
options: the fifth value, 19 — four values below it and four above

questions.question: Before finding any median, you must ALWAYS:
options: order the data — an unordered median is meaningless

questions.question: The mode of the dataset is:
options: 16 — the only value that appears twice

subtopics.title: Outliers and Choosing the Right Measure

questions.question: A tenth learner adds 130 minutes to the data. The mean jumps to:
options: 310 ÷ 10 = 31 minutes — with nine of the ten learners below it

questions.question: With ten values, the median becomes:
options: the mean of the fifth and sixth values: (19 + 22) ÷ 2 = 20,5
impossible to find for even counts

questions.question: The median is called RESISTANT to outliers because:
options: it uses every value in the dataset
it is always smaller than the mean
it responds only to position in the ordered list — an extreme value is just one more body at the end of the queue
outliers are removed before computing it

questions.question: For salaries at a firm where one director earns far more than everyone else, the best-justified report is:
options: the mean, because it uses every salary
the range, because it shows the gap
the median, because the data contains an outlier which distorts the mean

subtopics.title: Grouped Data and the Estimated Mean

questions.question: Why can the mean of the fifty grouped marks only be ESTIMATED?
options: The grouping destroyed the individual marks — fourteen learners sit somewhere in 70–80, but nobody knows where
Fifty values is too many to add

questions.question: The midpoint of the interval 40 to below 50 is:
With frequencies 6, 12, 13, 14, 5 and midpoints 45, 55, 65, 75, 85, the estimated mean is:
options: (45 + 55 + 65 + 75 + 85) ÷ 5 = 65 percent by coincidence, so no working is needed

subtopics.title: Modal Interval, Median Interval and Reading the Table

questions.question: With frequencies 6, 12, 13, 14, 5, the modal interval is:
options: 70 to below 80 — the class with the highest frequency, and the answer is the interval, not the 14

questions.question: Using cumulative frequencies 6, 18, 31, 45, 50, the median interval is found because:
options: the 25th and 26th values lie in the third class — the count was 18 before it and 31 by its end, so the median interval is 60 to below 70
the middle class of five is always the median interval

questions.question: The estimated mean (65) sits below the modal interval (70–80) because:
options: the midpoint assumption always lowers the mean
the tail of weaker marks in the forties and fifties drags the mean down

questions.question: The five-move method for any grouped table starts with:
options: auditing the frequency total — a miscounted table poisons everything after it

questions.question: In the three pictures, the mean is the pool-and-split because:
options: all the minutes are pooled and split perfectly equally — the only measure that touches every value
it is the biggest of the three answers

questions.question: Finding the median is like tapping the middle shoulder in an ordered queue because:
options: the middle person always has the average value
queues are used in statistics offices
you only order and point — the answer is the value of the middle position, with nothing added or divided
the median requires exactly nine people

questions.question: The tuck shop wants its bestseller, not an average flavour, because:
options: averages are hard to calculate for drinks
an average of orange and cola is not a drink anyone can buy — for categories, the most common value (the mode) is the useful answer
the mode is always the largest value

questions.question: When the 130-minute reader tips into the pool, the split becomes 31 minutes each. The problem is:
options: the newcomer read too little to count
nine of the ten learners read less than 31 — the share-out now describes almost nobody

questions.question: The newcomer joins the back of the queue and the median barely moves because:
options: the queue does not care how extreme the last person is — the middle position shifts by almost nothing
the queue re-orders itself around the newcomer
the newcomer is removed from the data

questions.question: 'Salaries at a company where the owner pays herself two million' calls for which thinking?
options: Pool thinking — the mean uses every salary
Queue thinking — the median, because the monster value wrecks the pool but not the queue

questions.question: Everyone in the forties crate is 'called 45' because:
options: 45 is the crate's most common mark
the crate hides the details, and the midpoint is the fairest single stand-in — errors above and below balance out
45 is the smallest possible mark in the crate

questions.question: The fullest crate — fourteen learners in the seventies — identifies:
Counting through the crates — six, then eighteen, then thirty-one — places the middle pair (25th and 26th) in:
options: the sixties crate, so the median interval is the sixties
the seventies crate, because it is fullest
